prompt: To answer HR questions, the app pastes the policy document into the prompt and says 'answer only from this'.
why: Giving the model the source text to answer from keeps answers tied to real content. That's grounding.
trap: It's an instruction, but the key is the supplied source.

prompt: The help bot looks up the right help articles first, then answers using them.
tells: looks up the right help articles first, then answers using them
why: Fetching relevant documents and answering from them is grounding, often called retrieval-augmented generation.
trap: Finding articles may use embeddings, but answering from them is grounding.

prompt: Answers include the page number of the manual they came from.
tells: the page number of the manual they came from
why: Pointing to the exact source shows the answer came from provided material. That's grounding.
trap: Citations guard against made-up facts, but here they show the grounding.

prompt: If the answer isn't in the provided files, the bot is told to say it can't find it.
why: Restricting answers to supplied files, and admitting gaps, is grounding.
trap: The aim is avoiding hallucination; the method is grounding.

prompt: A shop's chatbot answers using the store's own product sheets instead of general knowledge.
tells: using the store's own product sheets
why: Answering from the business's own documents is grounding the model in sources.
trap: It also works around the cutoff, but the clue is the source material.

prompt: Hallucinations dropped once the model was given the relevant records to read first.
tells: given the relevant records to read first
why: Supplying the facts to read reduces invention, because the model has the real answer in front of it. That's grounding.
trap: Wording didn't change; the input material did.
